title: Asymptotically attaining the Moore bound
abstract: Proves that, for each fixed positive diameter k, the largest order of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k is asymptotic to d^k as d tends to infinity. Constructs regular halved-flag graphs over every finite field, with exact order and diameter, a sharp degree cap, and matching asymptotics through all prime powers. Also proves the corresponding lower-limit bound for the edge extremum defined using line-graph diameter. Reusable infrastructure includes common bases for complete flags, odd-even sorting routes, exact flag enumeration, projective-line completion counts, and bipartite graph expansion. The analytic bridge retains the Wiener-Ikehara and prime-counting dependency closure from the Apache-2.0 PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project. The paper describes AI-assisted formalization supervised by the human authors.

informal.MooreBound.DegreeDiameter.theorem_1_1: For each positive natural k, n(k,d)/d^k tends to 1 as the natural degree bound d tends to infinity. Here n(k,d) is the maximum number of vertices of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k.
informal.MooreBound.DegreeDiameter.corollary_1_2: For each natural ell at least 2, the lower limit of h(ell,d)/d^ell is at least 1. Here h(ell,d) is one plus the maximum number of edges of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d whose line graph has extended diameter at most ell.
informal.MooreBound.DegreeDiameter.proposition_3_: For every positive k and prime power q, the concrete halved-flag graph is regular, has order [2k+1]_q!/(q+1)^k, degree at most (q+1)^k((q+1)^k-1), and extended diameter exactly k. Along all prime powers q tending to infinity, its actual degree divided by this cap and its order divided by the kth power of its actual degree both tend to 1.
informal.MooreBound.DegreeDiameter.alternating_ro: Any two complete flags in an n-dimensional vector space over a division ring admit an n-step route that changes only ranks of the prescribed alternating parity at each step.
informal.MooreBound.prime_between: For every positive real epsilon, every sufficiently large real x admits a prime strictly between x and (1+epsilon)x.
